reviews.title: No warning on deletions
reviews.text: The game just deletes your character after you invest so much time/money into it without warning because they keep on changing their ‘guidelines’ to be super pc even if they are private characters. At least give some warnings so we can change things around or at least refund some or most of the mats you use to build that character… I was on this game a lot because of the creativity it once had but now it’s becoming super limited. The real world is not just rainbows and unicorns that you can just filter into a box of checklists. Or there should be an adult/unfiltered section because of themes or what not. Don’t think I will be picking this up again unless it stops following the west’s movement of cringe. Great concept at first, but then fell into the normal traps of the west. Hopefully another company picks up the idea and makes it better.

reviews.title: Almost There
reviews.text:
The character creation and guiding the back stories has been my favorite part of this game. Battles are described beautifully and even. You have a chance in every battle. It doesn’t seem like an opponent has an overwhelming advantage even if they’re clearly from experienced players. 
There are a few things I’d like to see as the game evolves:
1. The AI script during adventures/dungeons is tedious and confusing. It’s not clear what your mission is and you can get caught in a loop, losing eternium (game currency)
The rest would probably take more programming than they’d be worth, but you never know…
2. I’d love to make teams of three or four with the same battle options and upgrades as duos. 
3. I’d love to be able to reference an already made character in the background story for a new one and have that relationship secured. You have to kind of force it right now. 
4. You should get one free picture change after the original character design. The AI makes people look similar and it takes a detailed description to make what you want. 
Overall this is fun and I want to see my characters succeed just as much as playing D&D with my friends as a kid.

reviews.title: Bug fix
reviews.text:
I’m getting tired of major bugs going unfixed. I’ve reported the broken ads for MONTHS. The X button does not work at all, forcing me to completely shut down the game and lose my progress.

The upgrade system has also wasted my currency. I spent upgrade points to raise an Epic piece of gear, the points were deducted, yet the item remained Epic. Now I’ve collected 18 item points from the login rewards over the last two days, but somehow I only have FOUR.

These aren’t cosmetic glitches. The game is taking earned currency, failing to award rewards, and forcing players to lose progress. I enjoy Taleborn, but this is becoming ridiculous. Please fix the core systems that are already broken before adding more content.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: This is definitely the best mobile game I've ever downloaded been playing for a while now and it just keeps getting better. Pick a realm (which they keep adding more they're up to 15 or 16 at the moment), then put in the description what you want your character to look like, what their personality is, speech patterns, and a little backstory, be as specific or vague as you want then hit generate and the AI will not only write a multi-paragraph and unique recent history for your character it will also generate a unique image, It also makes your character 100% unique skills to use in combat based on what you told it!! Then you make the full backstory!! It comes in 5 multi paragraph chapters you can pick a premade one or make a unique one by describing an outline of their backstory then the AI will generate one chapter at a time so you can read what it writes and if you like what it reads but want to change it slightly when you make the next chapter you get a chance to alter things before it generates. The game just keeps going though I'm very thoroughly impressed good job!!

reviews.title: The Idea of the game or Perfect
reviews.text:
The idea behind the game is incredible. Being able to create your own hero is an excellent feature and makes the experience much more immersive. I really enjoy the freedom and creativity the game offers.

However, the processing time for actions is way too slow. It takes too long for the game to process decisions and actions, which can make the experience frustrating and break the immersion. If the processing speed were improved, the game would be much more enjoyable.

reviews.title: Build Your Own Legend
reviews.text: Taleborn makes every character and adventure feel personal. I love creating original heroes, developing their stories, upgrading their skills and equipment, and testing different strategies in solo battles, duo fights, and dungeons. The battles feel cinematic, while the variety of builds gives me plenty to think about between fights. It’s imaginative, addictive, and unlike any other RPG I’ve played. I’m excited to see how it continues to grow!

reviews.title: Storytelling until the arena takes over
reviews.text: I enjoy coming up with an interesting concept and background and seeing how it writes the description and art. The basic background stories are quite cliche so I use a custom generated one. Guided stories can be fun as well, and you can write characters with interconnected backgrounds that reference other heroes you,have, though the system wants to write overly heavy emotions and it takes reminding every chapter to keep a different tone. In addition, the game steers everyone to this pan-dimensional arena setting, which means the last chapter and a half are always the same and take away significance of the origin worlds. A self-contained background ending within the chosen realm would be more interesting for those of us wanting story. The arena part appeals to me very little and I don't care about tournaments. I would rather continue stories in the realm I picked and feel like the hero exists in that setting.

This may be the first review I’ve ever given, but it is so well deserved. This game is genuinely the best game I have ever came across. Sure there are a few bugs, but what can you expect it’s a newer game by a solo developer. The dev releases updates nearly every day trying to fix bugs users notice. The dev truly cares about the users gameplay. Additionally I personally don’t think there are a ton of ads, ads are needed for the game to be free and I know a lot of games by bigger developers with 10x the amount of ads. Definitely give this game a go you can see how hard the dev works to improve the game for the users!

reviews.title: A good use of AI
reviews.text: I do a lot of world building in my free time, so I had a ton of characters i wanted to make, and the AI managed to get them about 80% accurate. There’s only so much it can do with a description, and u have to choose a premade realm for them to come from so that limits it a bit, but it’s understandable. There’s only so image generator is fine, but doesn’t work well for non human characters. My giant sea serpent randomly got arms and legs in a couple of its background stories, and I can’t get my plant parasite to look right. Other than these minor grievances the game is great. There’s only so combat system uses classes of skills (ex.pierce, or sweep) to choose who wins a fight, so you can’t just make an invincible character and just win, which is great because most of my characters are a bit more grounded than most others characters. I can’t wait to see what else the dev adds to it.

reviews.title: Not what I hoped for
reviews.text:
I love the idea of this game, but it took too long to get to the point where I actually got to play it. Instead of being able to play through with the character you create, you have to create two. Then you have to go through the origin story for each of those characters before you can do anything with them. This wouldn’t be so bad, except each one has five sections and you have to either wait several hours between chapters or pay tokens to skip the wait (limited number each day). 

I’m all for character creation but it took me four days to get through the first character build and I lost interest at chapter two of the second build. I never got past that, so maybe the game is fun but I’m too impatient to go through the whole process a second time

reviews.title: Pretty fun
reviews.text: I’ve been playing the game now for a little over a week maybe 2 weeks and it’s definitely been a fun distraction. Albeit, a ton of ads but that’s the price you pay for not subscribing or paying for anything by. The AI does a good job at creating your characters and giving them a fun story and even creating images and allowing you to alter the images as much as you can, so long as you know how to word things. The stories are fun and the fights are entertaining, you can skip the narrations if you want and you have 2 fights a day that are ad-free. Sometimes it feels like the AI has no logic but who am I to complain when it’s all made up anyways. I guess it adds some whimsy and keeps you from saying that your characters can never be killed or defeated so that it’s fun and fair for everyone. All around, fun game and easy to put down and let the ads run while you do another task
